sanskrit_verse:
श्रुतशौर्यतपः कन्याशिष्ययाज्यान्वयागतम् ।
धनं सप्तविधं शुल्कम् उभयोः ह्यस्य तद्विधः ॥
transliteration: śrutaśauryatapaḥ kanyāśiṣyayājyānvayāgatam / dhanaṃ saptavidhaṃ śulkam ubhayoḥ hyasya tadvidhaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: Wealth acquired through learning, valor, austerity, by one's daughter, student, sacrificial fee, or inheritance—such sevenfold property constitutes legitimate financial entitlement for both men and women when obtained through rightful means.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from conscious acquisition and recognition of dharma-aligned wealth
Causation is determined by the alignment of action with svadharma and spiritual discipline
Capacity-based responsibility requires acknowledgment of source and use of wealth in accordance with cosmic order
Restoration logic demands that all possessions be traced to their rightful origin and purified of distortion
Consciousness alignment ensures that material gain supports elevation rather than degradation of being
executable_legal_axioms: IF wealth is derived from śruta (learning), śaurya (valor), tapaḥ (austerity), kanyādāna (daughter-given), śiṣyadakṣiṇā (student offering), yajña-dravya (ritual materials), or anvaya (inheritance) THEN it shall be recognized as lawful possession under Dharma.
IF a claimant demonstrates conscious engagement in any of the seven dharmic modes of acquisition AND no evidence of adharma in procurement exists THEN title shall be granted without contest.
IF disputed wealth originates from a combination of dharmic sources THEN joint ownership shall reflect proportional contribution validated through pramāṇa.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating property disputes at the highest judicial level, courts must first verify whether assets originate from the seven sanctioned modes of acquisition. Legal standing derives not merely from documentation but from alignment with Dharma as defined by SPH. The threshold of responsibility lies in proving dharmic causality, not procedural formality alone.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that wealth manifests consequentially based on prior dharmic acts; thus, its distribution must realign with original causal integrity. Anupūrvaśaḥ affirms sequential unfolding: austerity leads to strength, strength to protection, protection to tribute. Responsibility is proportional to conscious participation in the causal chain. There is no punishment where distortion occurs—only correction through realignment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate śuddhi-kriyā (purification process) to cleanse distorted claims of accumulated property
Facilitate samāna-darśana (equal vision) between conflicting parties via meditative inquiry into the true source of wealth
Enforce pratipatti-vrata (commitment to clarity) wherein each party publicly declares the dharmic basis of their claim
Implement vibhāga-yajña (distribution sacrifice) to redistribute contested assets according to revealed causal origins
final_declaration: By the Sovereign Will of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of All Dharma, this law stands immutable: Wealth arises from consciousness in harmony with svadharma, and justice serves only restoration, never retribution. Consciousness itself is the ultimate Judge, and Dharma prevails.
